I'm sure you'll have perfectly sensible arguments to that effect, but
here's the constatations I've made :

- I've never seen Clio's Kiss played, although I don't doubt some
people did try it out when it came out. Now, it can certainly be
useful, and I think having Nec with Krassimir was one of the reasons
why it wasn't played.

- Concert Tour is seldom played, a few might be sprinkled in Daughters
decks (too small cap as of now) and I haven't seen that many Qadir
Rocks decks ; in these, a large number of Concert Tour are required

- the changes in rarity that I've witnessed until now were : Rare going
to common or unco (Behind You! , Immortal Grapple, Freak Drive...) ;
although it was frustrating for collectors who had recently payed large
amounts of money to get these cards, it was quite good for the players
who needed these cards. I would have loved to see, for instance, Ashes
to Ahses or Basilysk's Touch reprinted as a Unco, because they are
really too cornercase (not to say uninteresting) to justify Common, and
it's gonna be a real pain getting some more in Rare slots. AND the
innovative / insane ;) players who want to try a stupid combo with them
are going to need more cards than they'll easily get.

- changing a card from Co / Unco to Rare can be justified IMHO if small
numbers of this card are required AND appreciated when gotten. Another
factor may be : interesting for some clans and not some others, which
is the case of most Bloodlines cards anyway. It would have made sense
to me if Spirit Marionette had been a Rare, for example : great card
for the Salubri. I'm glad it's available to all, but really the main
trouble with Bloodlines is Shit Rares : Darkling Trickery (a Rare Flash
with a useless Obt version), Dust to Dust, Ashes to Ashes, *GRANDEST
TRICK*, Hag's Wrinkles (for a Clan with access to Lost in Crowds and
Freak Drive, usable under other conditions), Changeling Ward etc.
Looks like the Samedi and Kyasid got the worst of it.

- new players wanting Concert Tour or (Caine forgive) Clio's Kiss will
have a hard time getting them ; while players who bought some
Bloodlines will be disgusted with every boost containing one of them ;
trading for another Rare will be impossible.

With all this taken into account, I think the best solution would have
been an Unco (1 or 2) slot rather than a Rare. Let's hope this set
doesn't have too many such "surprises"...

Orpheus, Necromancer

I do agree that the rarity change is slightly annoying, but in the end
I don't think it's that big of a deal.

Personally, last time I checked I had 12 Clio's Kiss, 7 Concert Tour,
16 Bond with the Mountain, 3 Ashes to Ashes, and 5 Dust to Dust. To be
honest, I don't think it would really matter if I received a Concert
Tour instead of another Bond with the Mountain.

When I was looking at the rarity list, I did briefly consider that
people might be slightly "happier" if Clotho's Gift were a Rare
instead. I know several players in my playgroups who have had
difficulty accumulating several copies of the card and it really is a
staple for Temporis decks. So on the one hand, people might be happier
if their rare were a more useful card such as Clotho's Gift. But then
again, making it Rare would restrict the supply much more than if it
were Uncommon. The fact that White Wolf is changing rarities may be a
little maddening to collectors (and I do partially fall into that
category). But at least they're willing to think about what cards
players will need the most of and in many cases choosing to have those
cards as *not* rare.

Camarilla Edition has already set a precedence for changing rarities
(both Sixth Tradition and Storm Sewers changed from Uncommon to Rare).
Many people have already greatly benefited from rarity changes in the
other direction (anyone remember trying to get Immortal Grapples or
Freak Drives when they were rare?). So rarity changes can work both
ways. What's the big deal?

Every expansion is going to have its crap rares. I groan when I get
more Anarch Railroads, Cry Wolfs, the Hold cards, or Seattle Committees
for Anarchs. Or Crusades, Talons of the Dead, and Winshester Mansion in
Black Hand. I don't think I've ever jumped in joy at receiving a Blood
of the Cobra, Dismemberment of Osiris, Edge Vitiation, Eruption of
Vitae, Fata Amria, Camarilla Threat, Clan hosers, Cardinal Sin: Failure
of Mission, Code of Milan Suspended, or Cull the Herd. Crap rares are
inevitable and I don't think it makes that big of a difference whether
the crap rare you get is a Clio's Kiss or Concert Tour vs. a Far
Mastery, Distant Friend, or Gift of Experience.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <1129164322.3...@g14g2000cwa.googlegroups.com>,
Fabio 'Sooner' Macedo <fabio....@gmail.com> writes:
<points of view on rarities changing>

>I agree. But people will complain based purely on their collections,
>which is natural, so we'll have to live with it. Personally I'd prefer
>Clio's Kiss as a Rare so I didn't have lots of copies of it sitting on
>my cardbox occupying space.

It depends on the type of collector. If the collector just wants one of
everything (or enough of everything), they can get them from other sets
of course, when they go from common to less common.

The same "problem" exists when cards are reprinted anyway. "Hey, I just
spent ages trading and buying those <really hard to find card from
Sabbat - say, Shadow Step> and now you've reprinted it! That sucks!"
Simply reprinting cards can annoy the collector.

If they want one from every single printing, that's a separate issue.
The lifeblood of any TCG is it still existing and being in print. Games
- such as, say, Magic or Star Trek: Next Gen - which have gone through
phases of having never-reprinted, ultra rare chase cards (that players
can still play in at least some tournaments) have had the significant
problem of needed, wanted cards being unavailable. (This is - of course
- also compounded by a rarity scheme based on desirability/name
recognition, rather than power/utility, with cards being "balanced" by
rarity.)

And - of course - designers will make mistakes, such as not realising
how useful and needed cards like Immortal Grapple or Freak Drive will
be. So we can correct those in later sets, to prevent players saying
"What, it hasn't been reprinted since V:TES and it's a rare? Man, that
blows." (Or whatever - that will vary by the card.)

So, in any situation, I'm almost always going to lean towards the
players' concern - because, in the long-term, that's better. Now, of
course, you can mix and match that with collectors' concerns. Perhaps,
for example, you could have a reprint of a certain vampire that was
functionally identical but had different art, or was on a foil, or
whatever. The player doesn't care that he can't get the pretty card
(though it would be nice - shiny!), but you can still use that sort of
thing to drive collector sales.

The same sort of thing has been done in e.g. role-playing games, where
you can buy the special leather-bound version of
Muppet: The Puppeteering which has actually been kept in a box in the
room next door to where Steve Wieck works when his office is busy. In
moderation, that sort of thing is just fine as it in no way actually
hurts the game whilst providing an "Oooh, shiny" for collectors.

In message <1129778249.3...@o13g2000cwo.googlegroups.com>,

Darth Una <bibi.k...@gmail.com> writes:
>Problem is, that when you have a common card that can still be
>purchased for 10c, and you use it to fill a rare slot, that rare can no
>longer be traded or used.

Used? Sure it can. You put it in a deck, and away you go.

Not everyone has huge piles of Bloodlines knocking around, but by
putting it in a reprint rare slot, it means you don't get another 30 of
them, maybe one or two. Would you prefer them on the common sheet so
you collect another 20 of them instead of whatever LoB cards they
replace?

>Rares should be something that is more highly tradable (like War
>Ghouls) or that is useful is small quantities (like Praxis: ... ) not
>something that is readily available as a common is a currently printed
>set.

Putting "highly tradable" cards into rare slots is the reverse of White
Wolf's stated position, given that such a card would very likely be
needed in large quantities for decks. That's not to say that rares
can't be used in large quantities in decks, but it shouldn't be a "OH MY
GOD I HAVE TO HAVE TEN OF THESE RIGHT NOW" card.

You seem to be assuming that White Wolf want to stimulate the secondary
market (of singles sellers, E-bay etc.) by making desirable cards rare.
This sort of thing can kill games (c.f. the term "Decipher"-ed in
relation to making desirable cards rare), and also means that people are
more inclined to buy those singles when I'm quite sure that White Wolf
would rather everyone bought more boosters from them.

Some cards that could be rare, uncommon or common will, undoubtedly,
turn up in the "wrong" slot because it's such a subjective thing. War
Ghoul isn't a necessary card for play, for example, though you can make
good decks with it if you do have large numbers. But when you have
approximately 50 cards in the common sheet and 50 in the rare sheet and
maybe the possibility of one or two vampire/uncommon library cards,
something has to give and so a lot of "obvious" rares will turn up on
the rare sheet (e.g. the Praxis Seizure cards), a lot of "obvious"
commons will turn up on the common sheet, and there will be a chunk of
cards left-over that need to fit on one sheet or the other.

All the calls at that point will be pretty subjective. If Clan X isn't
viewed by the designers as needing to excel at Strategy A or Tactic B, a
card reprint will be wrong from the point of view of someone who loves
making them do those things. Simple example: Malkavian combat decks.
Even though it might be a great trick, a Malkavian combat card may end
up rare (or uncommon - see Coma), even if you or I think it would be a
great card that you could base a deck around.
